title: The lease is what keeps a claimed outbox row out of reach, on both engines
note: BUG-6 was an ASSERTION whose engine guard did not match the engine fact it was guarding. The racing test asserted the exact claim count behind `if connection.features.has_select_for_update` and then, with no guard at all, asserted that a follow-up claim returned `None`. On SQLite the two workers are serialised and the engine may refuse BOTH writes; nobody claimed the row, so it stays legitimately claimable and the unguarded assertion failed on a correctly-behaving system (measured here at 4 failures in 60 runs before the fix, all with the identical `AssertionError: 1 is not None`). The fix gates the trailing assertion on whether the row WAS claimed. M1 is the mutation that proves the guard did not become a shrug: with the lease no longer applied, a claimed row stays claimable and BOTH halves of the new assertion fire - the un-gated `assertIsNone` in the racing test on SQLite, and the un-gated `assertIsNone` in the new pin plus the exact-count invariant on PostgreSQL. Recorded because a guard that is never mutated against is how the original defect got in.

mutations.description: _claim stops pushing the row's next_attempt_at out by the lease, so the claimable predicate stays true for every other worker and a claimed row can be claimed again
